diff_hunk:
@@ -426,7 +426,8 @@
 			<return type="Variant" />
 			<param index="0" name="index" type="int" />
 			<description>
-				Returns the element at the given [param index] in the array. This is the same as using the [code][][/code] operator ([code]array[index][/code]).
+				Returns the element at the given [param index] in the array. Returns [code]null[/code] and prints an error if the access is out of bounds. Negative indices are not supported; they will always consider the value to be out of bounds and return [code]null[/code].
+				This is similar to using the [code][][/code] operator ([code]array[index][/code]), except that operator supports negative indices and causes a debugger break if out-of-bounds access is performed.
body:
Both with and without this PR, these descriptions are generally inconsistent with the corresponding `[]` accessor's descriptions, which I'm not sure how to feel about.

Though, in this PR specifically, they're too verbose for being so simple. An overcorrection for https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs/issues/10940 in my opinion. Also it's probably better to note here what **this** method can do, instead of what the operator cannot do.
```suggestion
				Returns the element at the given [param index] in the array. Returns [code]null[/code] and generates an error if the access is out of bounds. Negative indices are not supported.
				This method is similar to the [code][][/code] operator, except it doesn't pause the project execution if run from the editor.
```
or:
```suggestion
				Returns the element at the given [param index] in the array. If [param index] out-of-bounds or negative, this method fails and returns [code]null[/code].
				This method is similar to the [code][][/code] operator. Most notably, when this method fails, it doesn't pause the project execution if run from the editor.
```
Or similar.
Not a fan of _"pause the project execution if run from the editor"_ anymore but it's consistent.

Also applies similarly to the other descriptions.
